clue.text: Pirate at liberty to rob eastern wreck

parts.note: someone at liberty is free

indicators.note: to wreck the letters is to smash them into a new order

explanation.surface: A pirate, free to roam, sets about robbing a ship wrecked in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wreck' reads as a shipwreck in the pirate story, but it is the anagram signal for the letters that follow 'at liberty'.
explanation.definitionFit: A freebooter is a plundering adventurer, a synonym for a buccaneer or sea robber.

clue.text: Wife embraced by supporter is a dear, they say

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a supporter of a team is a fan

explanation.surface: A wife hugged by her admirer is told she is a darling.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on sound: 'dear, they say' is a deer, and the answer is a young deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A young deer still in its first year is called by this name, hence the pun on dear.

clue.text: In Bow he collected rent — an image-boosting activity

parts.note: in Bow, a Cockney district of East London, 'he' is said with its H dropped
to have collected something is to have got it
a rent is a tear or rip

explanation.surface: An East End landlord gathers the rent, feeling rather pleased with himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Bow' sets the Cockney accent of London's East End, where the H is dropped: 'E got rip.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an activity undertaken mainly to flatter one's own vanity and self-importance.

clue.text: Stern conductor's valet — an uncouth type

parts.note: the stern of a ship is its back
Sir Henry Wood was the conductor who founded the Proms; the 's gives the S
a valet is a manservant, a man

explanation.surface: A strict orchestra leader's personal servant turns out to be rather rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like an adjective for the conductor but is a noun, the back of a boat. Henry Wood was the British conductor behind the Proms concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from remote forest country is stereotyped as rough and unsophisticated.

clue.text: Escort free to enter ring

indicators.note: one piece is told to enter the other, so it goes inside it

parts.note: the outer is the outermost ring of an archery target
to free someone of something is to rid them of it

explanation.surface: A bodyguard is released into the boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests boxing, but it is the outer ring of a target.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcyclist riding alongside a dignitary's car serves as a guard or escort.

clue.text: Players accumulated one by one?

parts.note: a team of players, and also the figure 1 placed beside another 1 to make a two-digit number

explanation.surface: A team is assembled by picking players individually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one by one' means a 1 written next to a 1, giving the number of a cricket or football side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football side has this many players, and the numeral is two ones side by side.

clue.text: Blockbuster seen in the picture palace

indicators.note: the letters are seen inside the run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A big film is showing at the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: A picture palace is an old name for a cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockbuster film on a grand scale is described as an epic.

clue.text: An Asian riding up north has a stab at one

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a jockey who is riding is said to be up
a stab or punch is a jab
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Asian rider heading north has a go at something.
explanation.walkthrough: A jockey riding a horse is 'up'; 'up' in this down clue turns that into PU. 'has' and 'at' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Punjab region is an Asian, from India or Pakistan.

clue.text: They're employed to stop gentlemen running on the beach

definitions.text: They're employed to stop gentlemen running on the beach

parts.words: They're employed to stop gentlemen running on the beach
parts.note: 'gentlemen' was old slang for smugglers, and 'running' is smuggling contraband ashore, so these officials patrol the shore

explanation.surface: Staff are hired to stop men jogging along the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gentlemen' was an old name for smugglers, and to run goods is to smuggle them, so this is a shore patrol, not a fitness ban.
explanation.definitionFit: The shore patrol service watches the seaboard to prevent smuggling and aid vessels in distress.

clue.text: He may be axed for bringing down planes

definitions.text: He may be axed for bringing down planes

parts.words: He may be axed for bringing down planes
parts.note: reads like a pilot or gunner sacked for crashing aircraft, but planes are trees felled with an axe

explanation.surface: Someone faces the sack for shooting down aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Planes are plane trees, and 'axed' is literal: he wields the axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A forester who fells trees with an axe does exactly this to plane trees.

clue.text: She was a copper, once, in Bombay

definitions.text: was a copper, once, in Bombay
definitions.meaning: a former Indian coin, a sixteenth of a rupee, made of copper

explanation.surface: A woman served as a police officer in old Bombay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer, but it is a copper coin of British India.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, and also an old coin of the Indian subcontinent, a sixteenth of a rupee.

clue.text: Confusion caused by rowdier people in punt

indicators.note: the pieces go in the other word, enclosed by it

parts.note: a punt is a bet
rowdier means wilder
men are people

explanation.surface: Chaos is caused by rowdier passengers in a punt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests a boat but means a wager, BET.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewilderment is a state of perplexity or confusion.

clue.text: Rugby schoolboy mostly at the top

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Tom Brown, hero of Tom Brown's Schooldays, was a pupil at Rugby School

explanation.surface: A Rugby pupil is mostly top of the class.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Brown is the boy hero of a Victorian novel set at Rugby, an English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: The brow is the top of something, as in the brow of a hill.

clue.text: Graceless but trendy member in unusually neat apparel

parts.note: something trendy is in

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, as if dressed in it
unusually means the letters are arranged in a strange order

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Someone is clumsy despite fashionable legs in oddly tidy clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' signals the anagram, giving EANT; 'apparel' finishes the picture of a limb dressed in clothing and is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking grace or refinement is a near synonym of clumsy or awkward.

clue.text: Creature in the West, edible when cooked

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are mixed up as in a recipe

explanation.surface: An animal out West is tasty once it is cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cooked' rearranges WEST and EDIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu is an African antelope, a large grazing animal.

clue.text: Wrongful claim to professional status by …

parts.note: a claim to be professional is "I'm pro"
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: Someone falsely claims expert standing on the strength of what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue with the next, but each stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseemly or not in accordance with rules, as in misconduct, is a sense of wrongful.

clue.text: … Military Intelligence officer detailed for this location

indicators.note: detailed means the word loses its tail, its final letter

parts.note: Lieut is the short form of lieutenant, an army officer

explanation.surface: A Military Intelligence officer is posted to this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like being assigned a duty, but it means de-tailed: LIEUT loses T.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is a social setting or environment.

clue.text: Capital cover for a speculator's family

parts.note: a bear is a stock-market speculator who sells expecting prices to fall
kin are family

explanation.surface: A trader's relatives need protection in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' means of the head, not a city: the tall fur hat of guardsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital means relating to the head, and this tall fur hat is worn by British guards.

clue.text: Sleepy old quarters in dreary surroundings

indicators.note: one set of letters is placed in the other, which surrounds them

parts.note: dreary means dull, or dry
W and S are two of the compass points, or quarters

explanation.surface: A drowsy person dozes in run-down old lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' suggests lodgings but means compass points, W and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Half asleep and heavy-eyed means the same as sleepy.

clue.text: Point of view of 7 extremists invading plant

indicators.note: something invading another goes inside it

parts.note: an onion is a vegetable plant
the clue at 7 is an Asian of the Punjab; the first and last letters of that answer are P and I

explanation.surface: A view is formed about extremists invading a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' points to the answer at 7 down; its first and last letters go into ONION.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or belief that someone holds.

clue.text: Principal belongings, including 17, perhaps

parts.note: the head is the principal of a school
gear means belongings or kit

explanation.surface: The headmaster's belongings include a tall fur hat.
explanation.walkthrough: '17' points to the answer at 17 down, a guard's tall fur hat, an example of this; 'perhaps' marks that.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardsman's tall fur hat is one example of something worn on the head.

clue.text: Fugitive takes cover in English diocese

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
a cap is a head covering

explanation.surface: A runaway hides in an English bishop's area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' suggests hiding, but it is headwear; a see is the district a bishop governs. 'takes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has broken out of custody is a runaway or fugitive.

clue.text: Doctor's intention to go outside and climb tree

indicators.note: the reversed word is told to go outside the other, surrounding it
climb in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an intention is an aim
MO is a medical officer, a doctor; the 's gives the S

explanation.surface: A doctor means to go outdoors and climb a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climb' in this down clue turns the intention upwards, giving MIA, and 'to go outside' wraps that round the doctor's.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia known as wattle, with fluffy yellow flowers, is this tree.

clue.text: Officer takes note from robber? That's right

indicators.note: takes means the letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a brigand is a robber
i.e. means that is

explanation.surface: An officer takes a banknote from a thief, which is fair enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes ... from' removes N from BRIGAND, leaving BRIGAD.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an army rank of officer, above colonel.

clue.text: Lively fish caught in the interior

indicators.note: something in the interior of another sits inside it

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A lively fish is caught deep inland.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy means lively or spirited, vigorous in style.

clue.text: Sounds like a folklorist of severe aspect

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is spoken the same as the word given

parts.note: the Brothers Grimm collected German folk tales

explanation.surface: A collector of folk tales looks stern.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim means stern or forbidding in appearance.

clue.text: Monarch popular in old Ireland

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a monarch
popular means in

explanation.surface: A monarch is well liked in old Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Erin is the poetic, old name for Ireland.

clue.text: Canal employee identified by hair and ring

parts.note: a lock is a tress of hair
a keeper is a ring that holds another ring in place on a finger

explanation.surface: A canal worker is identified by hair and a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: A keeper ring is worn to guard a more valuable ring.
explanation.definitionFit: This canal worker operates the gates that raise and lower boats.

clue.text: Race to capture opponents' shelter

indicators.note: the race is told to capture the other piece and hold it inside

parts.note: TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
in bridge, East and North are opponents, partners being N-S and E-W

explanation.surface: Racing to take the opposition's cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race; bridge players East and North are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent is a portable canvas shelter.

clue.text: Prevailing trend changed in Amsterdam after loss of Dutch capital

indicators.note: changed means the letters are rearranged
after the loss of means one letter has gone from the word
the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the capital letter of Dutch is its first, D

explanation.surface: The dominant fashion shifted in Amsterdam when it lost its status as capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch capital' looks like Amsterdam itself but is just D, taken from AMSTERDAM; 'changed' mixes AMSTERAM with IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainstream is the dominant current of opinion or fashion.
